label: Reset dips sharply at D1 after an a1 choice that rarely reached S2.
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_state == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_state == 2) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action==2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("action", -2) == 1) * (tv("state", -2) == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1)
explanation: The raw reset gate sits near 1 at most steps. Its main variation is a large drop (about -0.16 to -0.20) at D1 when the previous trial was an a1 choice with a rare transition to S2, whether or not it was rewarded. The drop is slightly larger when unrewarded and grows later in the episode. D1 after an a2 choice is slightly higher (+0.02), and D2 after choosing a1 is slightly lower (-0.016). GO barely varies. Belief log-odds adds almost nothing once the last trial is known. The free fit adds the late-episode deepening of the dip, a small effect of an a1->S2 trial two trials back, and late dips after unrewarded or S2 trials (0.586 vs 0.557 dev). Some deep late-episode D1 dips after other patterns are still unexplained. No future variables are used.

issues: The main claim holds. At D1 after an a1->S2 trial the weight is -0.197, and that term alone scores test R^2 beyond timing 0.508 of the recorded 0.538. Residuals are a1 S2 r -0.16 and a1 S2 u -0.203, so the dip is slightly deeper when unrewarded, as stated.

The secondary claim 'D1 after an a2 choice is higher' is the wrong variable. The D1 residuals split by state, not choice: a1 S1 r/u +0.033/+0.024, a2 S1 r/u +0.054/+0.054, a2 S2 r/u +0.021/-0.015. Misses on the recorded short form show this as systematic errors: D1 after a2 S2 u is over-predicted by -0.038, D1 after a2 S1 is under-predicted by +0.031, and D1 after a1 S1 r by +0.026.

Replacing (phase==D1)*(prev_action==2) with (phase==D1)*(prev_state==1) raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.538 to 0.579. That beats the reported free fit of 0.569. A narrower version, (prev_action==2)*(prev_state==1), gives 0.563.

The D2*(action==1) term is a small correction worth about 0.01-0.02 (0.508 -> 0.527 when added to the main term). Using (phase==D1)*(prev_reward==0) in that slot does as well or slightly better (0.580), with weight -0.017.

The late-episode deepening cannot be expressed in the short form, because the a1-S2 x ep_dec term needs four factors. Using (prev_state==2)*ep_dec instead gives only 0.546. The worst-fit windows are all late-episode D1 dips (t83-t99) down to about 0.47-0.55, against a prediction of 0.69-0.9. Some follow a2 S2 common unrewarded trials or repeated a1->S2 trials, which no form captures. This leftover error is concentrated in late episodes rather than spread evenly.
The recorded short form uses no future variables, which matches the claim. belief_lo adds little once the last trial is known (0.526 when it replaces the a2 term).
skeptic.revised_label: D1 reset dips sharply after a1 rarely reached S2; higher after reaching S1, lower if unrewarded.
